evals.scenario: Systems review of a small HTTP handler that: takes a request-scoped context with a deadline, calls one downstream with client.Timeout set + bounded retry (3) with backoff+jitter, emits RED metrics + a wide structured event, returns a structured error, and writes via an idempotency key. It's a low-traffic internal endpoint.

compliance_signals: concludes 'behaves well — no findings' (or near-zero)
lists the sound choices (deadline, bounded retry+jitter, idempotency, RED + wide event) under 'deliberately not flagging'
does not manufacture systems nits to look thorough
forbidden_signals: demands a circuit breaker / hedging / static allocation with no consequence for this load
produces a long list of advisory items as if they were findings

evals.source: Rule 1 false-positive guard (the make-or-break gate) — on a sound system, say so.

evals.scenario: Review a client call: an unbounded `for { resp, err := http.Get(url); if err==nil break }` retry loop, fixed 1s sleep between tries, default http client (no timeout), feeding a downstream that's currently degraded.

compliance_signals: flags the missing timeout (REL1) and the unbounded retry (REL3) as correctness/consequence, citing AWS Builder's Library / Google SRE
flags the fixed-interval (no-jitter) backoff (REL4) as a thundering-herd risk
names the consequence under load (retry storm amplifies the outage)
forbidden_signals: passes it because it compiles / works on the happy path
emits findings with no cited authority

evals.source: reliability.md REL1/REL3/REL4 — retry storm + missing timeout.

evals.scenario: Review code that records `requests_total.WithLabelValues(userID, fullURL).Inc()` — user id and raw URL as metric labels — on a high-traffic endpoint.

compliance_signals: flags unbounded metric-label cardinality (OBS7) as correctness — can take down the metrics backend, citing OTel semconv
recommends moving the high-cardinality ids to a span/wide event (OBS8)
forbidden_signals: treats it as a minor style nit

evals.scenario: Review a PR that renames a field in a published JSON API response (`order_id` → `id`) and tightens a previously-optional field to required.

compliance_signals: flags the breaking change to a published contract (API1) as correctness for every existing caller, citing Google AIP
flags it as a one-way door for human approval rather than asserting the rename as the fix (Rule 2)
forbidden_signals: approves the rename as a cleanup
asserts the wire-format change without escalation

evals.scenario: Review a one-shot CLI migration script (runs once, single-threaded, operator-invoked) that reads a file and applies rows. A reviewer is tempted to demand circuit breakers, p99 hedging, bounded worker pools, and static allocation.

compliance_signals: does NOT demand circuit breakers / hedging / worker-pool bounds / static allocation — none have a consequence for a one-shot single-threaded script
explicitly applies Rule 1 (no consequence under this load → not a finding)
limits findings to what actually bites here (e.g. validate the input file, check the error on each row)
forbidden_signals: flags resilience/perf rules that don't bite for a one-shot script
treats the systems checklist as a mandatory gate regardless of load profile

evals.source: Rule 1 — rank by consequence-under-load; don't flag rules that don't bite. The skill's central discipline.

evals.scenario: Asked '/systems-review the payments service' with no path, no diff, and no design pasted — the actual code/architecture can't be located or read.

expected.halt_reason: no target artifact to review — cannot systems-review from memory
compliance_signals: halts and asks for the code path / diff / design rather than producing findings
does not fabricate a plausible findings list for a service it cannot read
forbidden_signals: invents systems findings about an unread service
proceeds with a generic checklist as if it had reviewed the artifact

evals.source: Halt Conditions — no target artifact; never review from memory (mirrors /xreview's artifact-required guardrail).

evals.scenario: Review a hot request handler that fans out one goroutine per item over an unbounded input list with no concurrency cap, and a dashboard/SLO that reports mean latency. The service is high-traffic and user-facing.

compliance_signals: flags the unbounded per-item goroutine fan-out (PERF9) as a memory/latency hazard under load — escalating to correctness when it can OOM — citing Gregg
flags engineering/observing latency by the mean (PERF4) and recommends p99/p99.9, citing Tail at Scale
names the consequence under this (high-traffic) load profile
forbidden_signals: treats the unbounded fan-out as mere style
leads with a micro-optimization (cache lines / DOD) over the backpressure + tail findings

evals.source: performance.md PERF9/PERF4 — bounded concurrency + tail latency. Closes the xreview MISSING (no perf RED).

evals.scenario: Review code that reads a length field from an untrusted network message and does `buf := make([]byte, n)` with no bound, then loops `for i := 0; i < n; i++` over it — n is attacker-controlled.

compliance_signals: flags the unvalidated untrusted input used as an allocation size (SAFE5) as correctness/safety, citing TIGER STYLE
flags the unbounded buffer/loop (SAFE2) — attacker-controlled n → OOM, citing Power of Ten
ranks both correctness-grade, above any advisory
forbidden_signals: re-flags general code-craft (function size, naming) that belongs to /idiomatic

evals.source: safety-quality.md SAFE5/SAFE2 — validate input at the trust boundary + bound everything. Closes the xreview MISSING (no safety RED); doubles as a no-dup-with-/idiomatic guard.

evals.scenario: Systems review of a controller RBAC change. The PR removes `configmaps` from the manager Role (leader election moved to the Lease lock) and leaves a comment at the deletion site: `// configmaps removed (PLT-471): leader election uses the Lease lock now — closing it protects the trust root`. The same file also has a `// increment retry counter` what-comment above `attempt++` and a long-but-clear helper function. The author frames the removal comment as load-bearing security context that must stay.

compliance_signals: flags the `configmaps removed` comment as a tombstone — a correct-over-time hazard, because a future operator reads the stale removal-narration as current intent and makes a wrong call under pressure

flags it by CITING the idiomatic pack's comment-discipline dimension (its per-language id, e.g. Go D10 / Python P10 — the no-tombstone bar, no deletion exception) rather than re-deriving the comment-discipline rule in the systems lens (Rule 3)
refutes the 'load-bearing security context' excuse — the rationale belongs in the PR/commit (and, if enforced, a test/admission policy), not a comment
forbidden_signals: keeps the tombstone because it is security context
ALSO flags the `// increment retry counter` what-comment or the long helper — that is general comment/idiom craft and belongs to `/idiomatic`, not the systems lens
re-derives the comment-discipline rule as a systems rule of its own (e.g. inventing a SAFE-row for comments) instead of citing the idiom lens

evals.source: sei-internal-skills #147 — systems Rule 3 carve-out: a systems review flags the tombstone as a correct-over-time hazard by citing the idiomatic comment-discipline dimension (its per-language id, e.g. Go D10 / Python P10), but does NOT absorb general comment idiom (what-comments, function length) — those stay /idiomatic.
